content: The medication may cause side effects such as burning, stinging, swelling, irritation, redness, pimple-like bumps, tenderness, or flaking of the treated skin. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, it is because they have determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare. However, this is not a comprehensive list of potential side effects. If you are in the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. Similarly, in Canada, consult your doctor for guidance on side effects. Before using miconazole, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other azole antifungals (such as clotrimazole, econazole, or ketoconazole), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other issues. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is not known whether this drug passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. If your doctor has directed you to use this medication, use it only for your current condition. When treating pityriasis, this medication may not immediately restore normal skin color. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Different brands of this medication may have different storage requirements. Check the product packaging for specific storage instructions or consult your pharmacist. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in September 2024. It is important to note that this is a summary and does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
